title: How much is all this costing? Like for people who are serious about gamedev
author: barret232hxc
selftext:
I was just curious how much all this costs. I haven't gone full in, been using cheap stuff like $10 opencode go and $20 cursor. But it seems like if you use Opus 5.5 you can do a lot, but how much is that going to cost you. 

Just was curious if people who have been doing this for awhile could share what they use and how much their monthly costs. is anyone getting any returns on these costs or is it mostly just a hobby. I see in my cursor plan using opus 5.5 eats up the tokens faster than pacman lol

I'm just trying to figure out the way to get the most bang for the buck and what options real devs are using, I see so many posts that do these crazy one shot games that say they spent thousands or something one prompt, is that really what everyone is doing or is that influencers bragging

comments.author: arangar
comments.body:
I'm in a similar boat as you, some observations.

If you pair program, you can do it way easier on the cheaper options - if you want to do all coding with AI, then the cheap ones will struggle.

I have a very strong macbook 128gb, but had a hard time geting local llms performing; you can get it to work pretty well, but they need more hand holing and are much slower than cloud models.

Swapping models for tasks, don't always use Opus is key - I had good result from free OpenCode models for simple tasks.

But if you are looking to do what people share in terms of "look at what I one shot" - Then that's not the $20 plans.

Edit: my idea was to have a Opus architect in a $20 drive coding on my local LLM; but so far I've struggled to get the local LLM hold up it's end of this bargain (I did some protyping, but it's been slow and stuck in long debugging loops).

comments.author: Sozobi
comments.body: My strategy is using the $20 Claude plan for the entire planning and brainstorming process of my game, getting every detail down from gameplay, story and all technical details I want in the game, all written into documents in the project folder. Then when I want to start on the actual coding work, I allow myself only a single month of the x5 Max plan. All the heavylifting and coding have to be completed within this month, and then it's back to the $20 plan from there for bug fixing, smaller addons and polish.

replies.author: Disastrous-Gain5870
replies.body: That’s actually a good plan for a tighter budget. I’ll keep that in mind! Though I feel like I’m too deep in now and I’m forced to spend $100 a month at the very least.

replies.author: Sozobi
replies.body: I would be able to keep it going for more months if I wanted to because I have the budget, but I just dont want to. I actually like having a sort of "time limit" or deadline, which forces me to make lots of progress during that one month instead of getting stuck in an eternal polishing loop. You could call it a self-imposed limiter of sorts. 🫡

comments.author: Carter5on
comments.body:
My latest project has been in development for 3 days and it will be in development until December this year. So, I would say €69 for Claude, €15 for ElevenLabs, €33,48 for Suno, €88,50 for Steam Fee. VAT included for all. In total €205,98. However, these subscription are there anyway, because I am using them for many projects.  
  
I am on Opus 5.5 medium. This will be my fifth solo-dev game, but my first where I am using AI for both programming and graphics. I'm a professional graphic designer, web designer, UI/UX designer and artist for games, so I can take care of the other sections of development and production with no cost.

comments.author: qqAzo
comments.body:
3 months in. Used Claude 10x for 3 months. ChatGPT (100usd) one for 1 month with a lot of resets. 1 month pro of Meshy.AI. Had a month where I did most the graphics.

Now I am back to Claude 10x + cheap ChatGPT. (while reloading new resets for ChatGPT)

**Future costs:** Epic games/Steam cost - maybe build a website to market the game - assets (I bought none - but feel animations is really a weak point with AI).

**Overall** I spent around 400 USD. Upcoming is 2x 100 for steam/epic, a domain might be 30 USD. My best guess is a beta release in 3-4 months. Final game in 6-7 months.

So a realistic pricetag on something that has depth, mechanics, multiplayer infrastructure, good graphics and can last longer than 20 hours played.

USD 1500 to reach a release button.

On a sidenote; Claude has estimated I need a 3.500 USD server to enable around 500 people online (around 120 concurrent matches). So the biggest cost as I see it comes with players. I made an arena game - which means I need a critical mass and most likely have to rent a server on release. Currently building out the server infrastructure and optimization is priority number one. That is in my eyes the biggest lever to reduce costs in a multiplayer game when using AI.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body:
I went full time game dev a couple of months ago, and here's what I'm spending.

Monthly  
$200 - Claude 20x   
$200 - Codex 20x  
$60 - Substance 3D  
$40 - Meshy  
$6 - Eleven labs

One Time  
$300 - High quality foley sound effects  
$400 - Blender plugins  
$2,000 - High end windows test PC (Nvidia) / dev worker  
$1,000 - mid range windows test PC (AMD) / dev worker  
$700 - monitors and peripherals for test machines

  
So monthly costs of $506 and one time costs of $4,400. This may sound expensive to some but it feels insanely cheap to essentially be running a one man game studio.

\* not counting the MacBook Pro I already purchased last year

replies.author: SeasawPhilosopher
replies.body: I've surveyed the market a bit, and if it's very successful, 100k+ copies isn't unreasonable at a $20 price. Subtract out the steam cut, probably will need to contract out some of the art, maybe get a publisher. Way too many variables at this point, but I don't really need the money anyway, which means I can just focus on making it the game I want and if I make a couple million that's amazing, and if I make $500 that would suck but I'll get over it and make the next game be better.

replies.author: andrewlewi
replies.body: Good mindset to worry about the game and not the money. IMO, that’s what game dev is all about. What’s the genre of your game?
